For the purpose of this statement it is assumed that all minable coal will be removed from both tracts as prices and technology increase during the next few years. The requirements of Montana law with respect to coal recovery are also relevant to the assumption that substantially all coal will be removed. At the above rate of development the coal reserves of Tract II (350 million tons) and Tract III (850 million tons) will be exhausted in approximately 2070 and 2040 respectively. For simplicity sustained levels of production and 100 percent recovery are assumed in determining the year of coal exhaustion.
In 1979 a second dragline will be added at the Tract III mine so that an annual production level of 10 million tons can be attained by 1982. Three draglines on Tract III by 1987 and one dragline on Tract II by 1981 would be required to attain coal production in accordance with the terms of the amended lease. With this equipment, coal could be mined at the rate of 15 million tons annually from Tract III by 1989 and 4 million tons annually from Tract II by 1982. Total production therefore from Tract II and III will be 19 million tons annually after 1989 under low development.
